newsitem.title: UK: Brit Gas drops legal action against Britain.
newsitem.headline: Brit Gas drops legal action against Britain.

text.p: British Gas said on Tuesday it will not proceed with legal action against Britain's Department of Trade and Industry (DTI) for repayment of gas levy.
"Following consultation with the DTI, the company is now satisfied that the gas levy legislation has been applied correctrly and will therefore not be pursuing its claim," British Gas said.
The tax wrangle between British Gas and the DTI became public in July when the utility announced it had issued a writ to recover "substantial" amounts of money from the government.
The DTI said at the time British Gas claimed to have paid about 1.0 billion stg too much under the gas levy Act, which was introduced in 1981
But a British Gas spokesman said today: "We will not be pursuing this claim."
British Gas had taken out the writ, which was never in fact served on the DTI, to keep open the opportunity of bringing the dispute to court if no out-of-court agreement could be reached.
"I am pleased that the matter has been put to rest without the need to resort to litigation," energy minister Lord Fraser said.

The gas levy currently obliges British Gas to pay four pence per therm of gas delivered to beach terminals from North Sea gas fields. The tax dispute focused on eight fields and 24 contracts between British Gas and exploration firms.
To cover its position, the DTI counteracted in July by taking out writs against gas producers so it could claim back money from them just in case British Gas would have to be repaid.
But the precautionary proceedings against the producers have now been dropped after the dispute with British Gas has been settled, the DTI said.
"We will not now have to proceed with the action against the producers which has been undertaken on a contingency basis to protect the taxpayer," Lord Fraser said in a statement.
The DTI said the gas levy matter was no completely closed, adding there were neither any talks with British Gas to modify the tax in the future.

"There were never any negotiations with British Gas because there was nothing to negotiate and as to what is happening with the levy in the future: there is no action that we are taking on it," a spokesman said.
